acceptanceCriteria.statement: A first-time visitor can understand that Notewright captures short notes within the first screenful of the landing route.
The primary note-capture action is visible and reachable on narrow mobile viewports without scrolling.
The note-capture input remains operable in a single-handed portrait grip.
A saved note is confirmed in place without navigating away from the capture flow.
The design does not reproduce the named reference’s wordmark, logo, exact copy, exact branded palette, or distinctive iconography.

accessibilityAndRecovery: Use explicit labels for the primary landing action and the save confirmation so state is not conveyed by icon shape alone.
Preserve draft text after interruptions or failed saves so the user can recover without re-entry.
Keep the capture field within thumb reach on mobile portrait layouts so one-handed use remains feasible.
Do not rely on color as the only signal for active, saved, or failed states.
If the landing hierarchy fails on a small screen, reduce supporting copy before hiding the primary action.
assumptions: The exact typography for Notewright is not specified in the brief; any type system choice should be treated as an implementation assumption until approved.

The visual treatment of the landing hero background is not specified beyond generic adaptation of the reference layout; any canvas color, texture, or illustration choice is uncertain and should remain provisional.
The note-capture screen’s control set is not fully defined in the brief; placement of auxiliary actions is an assumption as long as the capture field and saved confirmation requirements are met.
The brief does not provide actual screenshots from Notion or internal assets, so any further reference-specific visual interpretation is uncertain and should not be treated as fact.

principles: Use a left-aligned hero stack with one dominant CTA so first-time visitors can identify the product purpose before scrolling.
Keep the primary note-capture action visible on the landing screen at narrow widths instead of burying it behind secondary navigation.
Separate system chrome from content with stable boundaries and restrained elevation so the landing route remains legible in a single glance.
Carry a visible text label alongside navigation or entry controls where users are unlikely to memorize icon meaning on first visit.
Use structure and border treatment for separation rather than relying on heavy shadow or decorative surface effects.
Treat all non-sourced visual decisions as assumptions until validated against product content and actual implementation constraints.
globalDirection.summary: Adapt the public Notion homepage pattern only at the level of generic structure: a left-aligned headline stack, one primary action, and a short descriptive subhead on the landing route; keep the capture path immediately reachable above the fold and make the note-capture screen preserve input in a single-handed mobile grip.

accessibility: The headline stack must read in a single top-to-bottom order without relying on color alone to express hierarchy.
The primary CTA needs a visible text label rather than icon-only affordance so first-time visitors can identify the entry point.
Any supporting navigation must preserve its position and label visibility across viewport changes so orientation does not depend on remembered icon shapes.
failureAndRecovery: If the hero content exceeds the fold on small screens, reduce supporting copy before reducing the primary CTA’s prominence.
If the visitor does not understand the tool’s purpose, keep the one-sentence subhead explicit about note capture rather than adding secondary marketing claims.
If the primary action is missed, repeat the same destination once in a secondary on-page link only if it does not create a competing call to action.
mobileRules: primary note-capture action remains reachable above the fold on narrow viewports
screenBlueprints.summary: A landing route that follows the named reference only in its generic information hierarchy: left-aligned headline stack, one sentence subhead, and a single primary CTA that leads into note capture while remaining visible above the fold on narrow viewports.

accessibility: Keep the capture field reachable within thumb range on narrow screens so one-handed entry does not require stretching.
Expose the saved confirmation as text, not color alone, so the state change is perceivable without assuming hue discrimination.
Preserve focus and draft content after save so recovery from interruption does not require retyping.
failureAndRecovery: If the input overflows the viewport, collapse nonessential chrome before shrinking the editable area.
If saving fails, keep the draft in place and surface a retry action adjacent to the field.
If the saved state is shown, confirm success in place rather than redirecting away from the capture context.
mobileRules: capture input remains usable in a single-handed portrait grip
saved state confirms capture without navigating away
screenBlueprints.summary: A note-capture screen optimized for quick entry: the input remains reachable and operable in portrait single-handed use, and saved state confirms completion without forcing route changes.

sourceDecisions.rationale: The brief explicitly names the public Notion marketing homepage layout with a left-aligned headline stack as a safe generic pattern to adapt; this is the only reference-level structural choice clearly grounded in the case brief.
A single primary CTA is directly supported by the brief’s named reference layout and aligns with the need to get the visitor from landing to capture without extra decision points.
The landing screen must keep the primary note-capture action reachable above the fold on narrow screens, so the hero decision should not be displaced by secondary controls.

Border-led separation can support readable structure without reproducing the reference’s proprietary palette or iconography; this is appropriate for a fictional product that needs clear orientation on landing and capture screens.
Low-elevation or no-elevation framing keeps the attention on the content rather than on container chrome, which suits a note-taking entry path where the field itself matters most.
Visible labels alongside controls support first-time visitors who cannot be expected to recognize icons immediately, which is relevant to a landing route and a capture entry path.
The brief explicitly forbids reproducing the named reference’s wordmark or logo, so no proprietary identifier from the reference may be carried into the design.
The case brief forbids proprietary copy from the named reference, so headline, subhead, and CTA wording must be original and only structurally inspired by the source pattern.
The brief explicitly disallows Notion’s exact black-and-white branded palette and its distinctive typographic choices, so those values cannot be replicated.
Distinctive iconography from the named reference is off-limits, so any controls must use generic or original symbols and cannot echo the source visual language.
